Okay, I need to figure out who the President of the United States was when the United Nations was established. Let me start by recalling when the United Nations was formed. I think it was after World War II. The UN replaced the League of Nations, which didn't work out after World War I. 

I remember that the UN's founding date is October 24, 1945, when the Charter was ratified by the majority of the original signatories, including the five permanent members of the Security Council. Now, who was the U.S. President then? Franklin D. Roosevelt comes to mind, but he died in April 1945, right? So he was President during most of the war, but he passed away before the UN was officially established.

That means the next President, Harry S. Truman, was in office when the UN was formed. FDR died in April, and Truman took over as President. So the key dates to check are FDR's death and when the UN was officially created. Let me confirm: FDR's presidency was March 4, 1933 – April 12, 1945. Truman was president from April 12, 1945, onward. The UN was established in October 1945, so Truman was President then. 

I should also make sure that the UN's formation date is correct. The Charter was signed in June 1945, but it came into effect on October 24 when ratified. So the United States, as one of the signatories, would have been under Truman's leadership then. Therefore, the answer should be Harry S. Truman.
[/Thinking]

Yhdysvaltain presidenttinä Yhdistyneiden Kansakuntien muodostamishetkellä oli **Harry S. Truman**. Hänestä tuli presidentti vuonna 1945, kun Franklin D. Roosevelt kuoli virkaansa huhtikuussa 1945, ja UN:n virallinen perustamispäivä oli 24. lokakuuta 1945.
